bullets.title: IBM pre-announcement triggers sector rotation: semis/memory up, software down
bullets.body: IBM reported preliminary Q2 revenue of $17.2B (vs. $17.86B est.) and EPS of $2.27 (vs. $3.02 est.), blaming client capex shift toward servers, storage, and memory ahead of supply-constrained price increases. This drove MSFT -2.8% premarket, ADBE -5.6%, INTU -7.3%, NOW/CRM/SNDK in sympathy; while MU +5.2%, STX +5.7%, WDC +6.1%, DELL +3.6%, SMCI +2.1% rallied. JPMorgan maintains Overweight at $290, calling the miss idiosyncratic to mainframe/Z systems; Citi keeps Buy/$375 PT; HSBC downgraded to Reduce with $191 PT.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: IBM capex shift bullish for AVGO, TSMC, memory semis; software names (WDAY, TEAM, HUBS, NOW, CRM) down 5%+
bullets.body: MS TMT notes enterprise IT services and software broadly lower in IBM's wake (WDAY, TEAM, HUBS, NOW, ACN, INFY, CRM, INTU down 5%+) while AI capex/semis outperform (SNDK, ALAB, AMAT, WDC, GLW up 5%+). AVGO retains ~80% of GOOGL TPU revenue despite MediaTek displacement fears; MS reiterates OW with $502 PT (~30% upside). TSMC expects Q3 revenue up low-to-mid teens q/q, raises FY26 guidance to high-30s% growth, capex to high end of $52-56B; 2nm demand 60kwpm above plan.

bullets.title: NVDA/AMD: US grants licenses for H200 and AMD AI chips to ZTE, Kingsoft, Maginfra; NVDA-Mitsubishi data center cooling partnership
bullets.body: The US granted export licenses to Chinese firms ZTE, Kingsoft, and Maginfra to purchase NVIDIA H200 and AMD AI chips, signaling potential easing of China chip restrictions. Separately, NVIDIA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries are considering a partnership focused on cooling and power systems for data centers per Nikkei.

bullets.title: TSEM surges ~19% premarket on ~$3B Japan government investment for chip manufacturing expansion
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor shares jumped 18.6% in premarket trading after announcing approximately $3B in Japanese government investment supporting capacity expansion in silicon photonics and germanium. At least one trader noted long exposure via Jan 2028 $410 calls.

bullets.title: ASML preview: Jefferies flags need for 90+ low-NA EUV unit guide to avoid de-rating; stock at elevated 50x FY26 multiple
bullets.body: Jefferies warns ASML must guide for at least 90 low-NA EUV systems to support the stock ahead of Wednesday's results; anything below triggers a decline. The stock trades at 50x FY26, 38x FY27, 32x FY28 consensus EPS after a 66% re-rating since Sept 2025. China sales risk from MATCH Act (20-30% decline, ~20% of sales) and hyperscaler capex shortfall concerns add de-rating risk.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley raises hyperscaler capex to $1.4T by 2028; META, AMZN, GOOGL top beneficiaries
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak raised hyperscale capex forecasts to ~$1.2T in 2027 and ~$1.4T in 2028 on 4x compute capacity growth from 2025-2028, with new cost-per-GW math supporting upward revisions across META, AMZN, and GOOGL. Separately, MS QDS notes memory shortage is durable through 2030+ (confirmed by NVDA and SK Hynix CEOs), GPU rental rates up 5-10% in July, and hedge funds saw the largest two weeks of tech hardware/semis buying on record.

bullets.title: NFLX Q2 preview: consensus $12.58B rev, 32.8% op margin; MS lowers PT to $90, flags churn post-price hike
bullets.body: Netflix reports 7/16 after close; consensus expects $12.58B revenue (+13.5% YoY) and EPS $0.79 vs. $0.78 guidance. Morgan Stanley lowered PT to $90 (from $115), reiterates OW but notes higher-than-normal churn per credit card data post-price hike and expects only inline results with low single-digit engagement growth. JPM names NFLX a top pick for Q2 internet earnings season.

bullets.title: AAPL: KeyBanc downgrades to Underweight/$250 PT; MS sees strong iPhone pricing power with $200 hike likely for iPhone 18
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded Apple to Underweight with a $250 price target, calling the stock near peak. Contrarily, Morgan Stanley argues iPhone demand shows 0.2-0.5 elasticity (most inelastic product in lineup) and models a $200 price hike for iPhone 18, driving +2-4% F3Q EPS upside and +1% FY27 upside; build plans on track and Apple is pursuing Chinese memory suppliers to preserve margins.

bullets.title: NY data center moratorium (50MW+): Citi keeps Buy on EQIX, DLR, WULF; WULF projects unaffected
bullets.body: New York Governor Hochul signed an executive order banning new large data center construction (50MW+) for up to one year, the first such statewide action. Citi maintains Buy on EQIX (top pick), DLR, and WULF; WULF's Lake Mariner project is unaffected as it doesn't require DEC permits. The supply constraint could benefit operators able to proceed; regulatory copycat risk from other states is flagged.

bullets.title: NBIS: Nebius secures $1B+ AI compute deal with Reflection AI through 2029
bullets.body: Nebius Group agreed to sell over $1 billion in AI computing capacity to Reflection AI under a contract extending through 2029, marking a major revenue visibility event for the company.

bullets.title: META/GOOGL/AMZN internet checks ahead of earnings: MS rates sector Attractive; GOOGL seeding TPUs into Neoclouds
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes META +15% on the day, trading at 20x '26 EPS (15% below TTM avg); AMZN at 26x, GOOGL at 24x. GOOGL is seeding TPUs into third-party Neoclouds to challenge NVDA's AI infrastructure control using financial backstops and lease commitments. META 2Q expected +34% y/y with Business Agents tailwind from 3.5B DAUs. JPM top picks for Q2 internet: GOOGL, AMZN, SPOT, DASH, NFLX.

bullets.title: ARM: KeyBanc raises PT to $430 from $300
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised its ARM Holdings price target by 43% to $430 from $300, reflecting improved earnings outlook.

bullets.title: MDB: DA Davidson pre-quiet check sees Atlas growth at 28-29% YoY vs 26% guidance; Vector Search now GA
bullets.body: MDB is sounding upbeat ahead of earnings with DA Davidson expecting Atlas YoY growth of 28-29% vs. the 26% guided, consistent with 220-340bps typical upside. MongoDB's Vector Search on Enterprise Advanced became GA June 30 and enterprise AI workload negotiations are underway.

bullets.title: CRWD/PANW/OKTA pre-quiet period checks: security demand pipeline at 4-year high; PANW walking down FCF margin
bullets.body: DA Davidson's pre-quiet period channel work shows record VAR demand for security software with pipeline strength at highest in 4+ years. CRWD EDR growth accelerating for three consecutive quarters on AI-driven AV displacement; PANW anchoring FY27 adj FCF margin to 37%+ vs consensus 37.9%; OKTA CRPO expected to accelerate to 13%+ vs 12% guidance.

bullets.title: ANET, CLS, LITE: UBS flags strong orders and backlog for data center networking; supply constraints may cap upside
bullets.body: UBS previews Q2 for enterprise hardware and networking: robust demand for data center networking switches supports ANET and CLS quarters and outlooks, but increasing lead times for key components could limit revenue upside. LITE expected to grow from Components and Systems despite supply chain constraints.

bullets.title: EFX: UBS Buy/$220 PT; credit bureaus well-positioned with consumer credit resilient despite mortgage headwinds
bullets.body: UBS rates EFX Buy at $220 PT (~11.8x FY28E EBITDA), citing Workforce Solutions (~40% of revenue) and housing recovery optionality. FICO rated Neutral/$1,320 PT; TRU Neutral/$80 PT. Consumer credit card loans rose 4-7% YoY across major banks; 30-yr mortgage rates at ~6.5% remain a headwind for H2 2026.

bullets.title: RCL/CCL/DIS cruise: UBS channel check shows mid-single-digit growth; Q1'27 pricing positive across all brands
bullets.body: UBS's cruise channel check shows North American demand tracking mid-single-digit bookings growth in June-July, unaffected by Middle East volatility. European-sourced demand for European itineraries remains weak (World Cup impact, fuel concerns). Q4'26 pricing: RCL +3% YOY, DIS +8% YOY; Q1'27 across all brands positive: RCL +3%, Carnival +4%, Disney +7%, Norwegian +1%.

bullets.title: CVNA: JPMorgan maintains Overweight; expecting modest 2Q beat with 2H EBITDA growth trajectory as key watch
bullets.body: JPMorgan maintained Overweight on CVNA, expecting a modest 2Q26 beat from better pricing dynamics. The return to EBITDA-per-unit growth in 2H26 is flagged as the critical forward catalyst for sustaining momentum.

bullets.title: DKNG: Kalshi prediction market court losses create regulatory overhang; Supreme Court timeline extends to late 2027-2028
bullets.body: Kalshi lost preliminary injunctions in New York and faces restrictions in Nevada, Michigan, and Massachusetts with more states likely. Citi views prediction markets as material but not overwhelming incremental growth for DKNG and FLUT. Congressional resolution is unlikely post-2026 midterms; Supreme Court ruling not expected before late 2027 at earliest.

bullets.title: NFLX/DIS/WBD: Morgan Stanley streaming survey — Netflix leads on retention and originals; DIS/NFLX Overweight
bullets.body: MS AlphaWise streaming survey shows average US household has 5+ services; Netflix has strongest net retention and best original content perception. Disney+/Hulu, Paramount+, and HBO Max saw solid engagement gains. MS rates DIS Overweight, NFLX Overweight, WBD Equal-weight, AMCX Underweight.
